title: Web
tagline: Build a page, style it, make it mobile-friendly and publish it.

lesson.p: HTML describes a page's content with tags. A page has <html>, <head> (invisible info) and <body> (what you see).

a heading,

a paragraph, a link, an image,

  • a list.

Most tags open and close:

alt describes the image: useful when it doesn't load (weak connection) and for visually impaired people.

Which tag makes a link? (one letter)
What is an image's alt attribute for?
options: Describing the image if it doesn't show
exercises.why: alt shows in place of the image and helps accessibility.

exercises.q: What happens if you forget to close a tag?
exercises.why: The browser guesses wrong and renders it crooked.

lesson.p: CSS describes looks: colours, sizes, spacing, fonts. It is made of rules: a selector and properties.
p targets paragraphs, .card targets the “card” class, #top targets the “top” id. Classes are the most used.
Every element is a box: content, padding (space inside), border, margin (space outside).
display:flex lines items up in a row or column and handles space easily. It is the base of modern layouts.

exercises.q: Which language handles colours and appearance?
Which property adds space inside a box?
exercises.why: padding = inner space, margin = outer space.

exercises.q: Which display value lines items up easily? (one word)
Which rule turns h1 headings green?
exercises.why: A selector then properties in braces.

exercises.q: Connect each property to its effect.
exercises.why: Each property has a precise effect.

lesson.p: Most of your visitors are on phones. The viewport tag (<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">) fits the page to the screen. Without it, the page looks tiny.
A too-heavy image slows everything, especially on little data. Compress them and pick suitable dimensions.
A link or image that doesn't show is often a wrong path (img/photo.jpg vs Img/Photo.JPG: case matters on the server).
A static site is published by sending your files to GitHub then Netlify: each upload updates the site. Always test on a phone first.

exercises.q: What is the viewport tag for?
options: Fitting the page to the screen size
exercises.why: Without it, the page is tiny on mobile.

options: So the page loads faster and uses less data
exercises.why: A light image loads fast, even on a weak network.

exercises.q: An image doesn't show. First check?
options: The path and the filename's case
exercises.why: The path or the case is often the cause.

exercises.q: On which kind of device must you always test before publishing? (one word)
Put in order to publish an update.
What is the benefit of a light static site?
options: It is fast and cheap to host
exercises.why: Few files, fast loading, simple hosting.

lesson.p: Clients send you 8 pages. 4 have a bug. It's up to you to find each bug with the render, the code, the console and a phone test.
Look at the render, read the code, open the console (it flags missing files), then test on a phone. Then pick the right fix.
Rewriting everything or changing host almost never fixes a simple bug. Find the precise cause.
